Seminar Title:

Towards Efficient and Secure Federated Learning: Adaptive Client Selection with Communication-Aware Quantization

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Name:

Speaker Type:

Contact:

Prof. Panthadeep Bhattacharjee, PIC Seminar

Abstract:

Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized data sources while preserving data privacy. However, real-world deployment of FL is hindered by significant challenges, including high communication overhead, inefficient client participation, and vulnerability to untrusted updates. This paper presents an efficient and secure federated learning framework that integrates adaptive client selection, model quantization, and cryptographic verification into a unified pipeline. The proposed adaptive selection mechanism dynamically prioritizes clients based on data diversity and historical reliability, ensuring informative participation while reducing redundant communication. To further optimize bandwidth usage, model updates are compressed using 8-bit quantization, achieving substantial reduction in transmission size with negligible impact on model performance. Additionally, digital signatures are employed to guarantee the integrity and authenticity of client updates, mitigating potential security threats. Experimental evaluation on a distributed fraud detection task demonstrates that the proposed approach reduces communication cost by up to 83.5% and improves training efficiency, while maintaining comparable accuracy to standard federated averaging. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining intelligent client selection, compression techniques, and security mechanisms for scalable and trustworthy federated learning systems.
